findings.evidence: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. findings.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.evidence: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.

extra.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: Cross-Domain Misconfiguration
findings.evidence: Web browser data loading may be possible, due to a Cross Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) misconfiguration on the web server.

extra.solution:
Ensure that sensitive data is not available in an unauthenticated manner (using IP address white-listing, for instance).
Configure the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" HTTP header to a more restrictive set of domains, or remove all CORS headers entirely, to allow the web browser to enforce the Same Origin Policy (SOP) in a more restrictive manner.

These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.

extra.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: Cross-Domain Misconfiguration
findings.evidence: Web browser data loading may be possible, due to a Cross Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) misconfiguration on the web server.

extra.solution:
Ensure that sensitive data is not available in an unauthenticated manner (using IP address white-listing, for instance).
Configure the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" HTTP header to a more restrictive set of domains, or remove all CORS headers entirely, to allow the web browser to enforce the Same Origin Policy (SOP) in a more restrictive manner.

extra.solution: This is an informational alert and so no changes are required.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.evidence: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797.

extra.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

correlate.executive_summary: The assessment found several informational and low/medium risk issues on https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/. An exposed directory /ftp was discovered and is explicitly disallowed in robots.txt but still returns HTTP 200, which warrants manual review. The site demonstrates a permissive CORS configuration (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) and missing security headers (HSTS, CSP, Referrer-Policy) that together increase the risk of client-side attacks. The application appears hosted on Heroku (heroku-router header and wildcard certificate); no product/version CVE matches were returned for the detected services.

findings.title: Exposed directory referenced in robots.txt: /ftp
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 200 on /ftp (differs from baseline 404); body sha256=b2b85673...; recon: robots.txt lists Disallow: /ftp (explicit lead). va (nikto): File/dir '/ftp/' in robots.txt returned a non-forbidden or redirect HTTP code (200) and "robots.txt" contains 1 entry which should be manually viewed.

findings.title: Missing important security headers (HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy)
findings.evidence: recon: Response did not set strict-transport-security. recon: Response did not set content-security-policy. recon: Response did not set referrer-policy.

findings.title: Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) appears permissive (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *)
findings.evidence: va (nikto): Uncommon header 'access-control-allow-origin' found, with contents: *; va (nikto, OPTIONS): Uncommon header 'access-control-allow-methods' found, with contents: GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE. va (zap): Cross-Domain Misconfiguration reported (web browser data loading may be possible due to CORS misconfiguration).

findings.title: Platform / server fingerprint: Heroku hosting indicators
findings.evidence: recon: Detected: Heroku (Server header: Heroku). va (nikto): Retrieved via header: 1.1 heroku-router; va (nikto): Server is using a wildcard certificate: '*.herokuapp.com'.

findings.title: Multiple uncommon or revealing HTTP headers present
findings.evidence: va (nikto) observed several uncommon or explicit headers: 'feature-policy' (payment 'self'), 'x-content-type-options' (nosniff), 'x-recruiting' (/#/jobs), 'nel' (report_to: heroku-nel ...), 'report-to' (heroku-nel endpoints), 'reporting-endpoints' (heroku-nel=...), and 'x-frame-options' (SAMEORIGIN). These headers may reveal implementation details or require review for correct configuration.

findings.title: Server ETag reveals inode-like values
findings.evidence: va (nikto): Server leaks inodes via ETags, header found with file /, fields: 0xW/2700 0x1a17c05cfd3.

findings.title: Cache-control directives should be reviewed
findings.evidence: va (zap): The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing browser and proxies to cache content. Recommendation: set 'no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate' for sensitive content or appropriate caching directives for static assets.

correlate.deduplication_notes: Merged multiple discoveries relating to the same underlying items: recon's '/ftp' discovery, the robots.txt Disallow: /ftp entry, and nikto's '/ftp/' 200 response were combined into a single finding about the exposed /ftp directory. Multiple nikto HTTP header observations were aggregated into one finding for uncommon/revealing headers rather than separate entries per header. The nikto and recon Heroku indicators (heroku-router header and wildcard cert) were combined into one platform fingerprint finding. The nikto robots.txt note was incorporated with the /ftp finding rather than reported separately.
